header.userPrompt:
Fix GitHub issue #5542: remove the `phase` attribute from the OpenTelemetry `http.server.request.duration` histogram, so that it is recorded exactly once per request, as the OpenTelemetry HTTP semantic conventions require (https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/http/http-metrics/#metric-httpserverrequestduration).

## Problem

Both OpenTelemetry metrics modules record the `http.server.request.duration` histogram twice per endpoint-handled request: once in `onResponseHeaders` with attribute `phase=headers`, and once in `onResponseBody` with `phase=body`. `phase` is not part of the semantic conventions, `count` of the histogram is ~2x the number of requests, and cardinality doubles. It is not exactly 2x: `onException` records once with no phase attribute, `onInterceptorResponse` records once with `phase=body`, so filtering on `phase=body` on the user side drops exception observations.

Affected files:
- metrics/otel4s-metrics/src/main/scala/sttp/tapir/server/metrics/otel4s/Otel4sMetrics.scala (`requestDuration`, `responseAttrs`)
- metrics/opentelemetry-metrics/src/main/scala/sttp/tapir/server/metrics/opentelemetry/OpenTelemetryMetrics.scala (`requestDuration`, `asOpenTelemetryAttributes` for responses)

The label originates from the Prometheus metrics (2022), where it must stay: Prometheus, Datadog and ZIO metrics use tapir-specific metric names and are NOT in scope. Do not touch them.

## Required changes

1. In `requestDuration` of both modules: remove the `onResponseHeaders` callback. Record the histogram once, on `onResponseBody`, plus the existing `onException` and `onInterceptorResponse` paths. Never add a `phase` attribute.
2. Remove the now-constant `phase: Option[String]` parameter from `Otel4sMetrics.responseAttrs` (package-private, used by the test) and from the response overload of `OpenTelemetryMetrics.asOpenTelemetryAttributes` (private).
3. `MetricLabelsTyped.forResponsePhase` / `ResponsePhaseLabel` in server/core must stay (other backends use it). Add a short note to its doc comment that the OpenTelemetry modules (`OpenTelemetryMetrics`, `Otel4sMetrics`) ignore it.
4. Update the doc comments on `OpenTelemetryMetrics.default` (two overloads) that currently describe the `phase` attribute; remove those sentences.
5. Tests:
   - `metrics/otel4s-metrics/src/test/.../Otel4sMetricsTest.scala`: `requestDurationExpectation` success branch expects `pointCount(2)` with `phase=headers` / `phase=body` points; change to a single point without a phase attribute. Remove the `phaseAttribute` helper. Adapt the `responseAttrs` call sites to the new signature.
   - `metrics/opentelemetry-metrics/src/test/.../OpenTelemetryMetricsTest.scala`: asserts `AttributeKey.stringKey("phase")` at ~lines 167 and 291; update so the duration histogram has one point per request, no phase key.
   - Add or adjust a test in each module that verifies the duration histogram's `count` equals the number of successful requests (this is the user-visible bug).
6. Docs: doc/server/observability.md — the OpenTelemetry and otel4s sections do not mention phase; verify and leave as is. Do not create a migration doc.
7. PR description must state this is a breaking change for anyone querying the OpenTelemetry duration histogram by `phase`, and reference `Fixes #5542`. Keep the PR description short and in simple language.

## Constraints

- Comments: only add what is not obvious from the code, keep them minimal.
- Compile and run tests for the Scala 2.13 and Scala 3 variants of the two modules: `sbt "opentelemetryMetrics/test" "opentelemetryMetrics3/test" "otel4sMetrics/test" "otel4sMetrics3/test"` (sbt-projectmatrix ids; `opentelemetryMetrics` also has a 2.12 variant, `opentelemetryMetrics2_12`, which must compile too).
- Do not add Claude as a co-author on commits.

resultJson.description:
Fixes GitHub issue #5542. The two OpenTelemetry metrics modules (`tapir-opentelemetry-metrics` and `tapir-otel4s-metrics`) record the `http.server.request.duration` histogram twice for every endpoint-handled request: once when response headers are ready (attribute `phase=headers`) and once when the body completes (`phase=body`). The OpenTelemetry HTTP semantic conventions require exactly one observation per request and define no `phase` attribute. As a result the histogram `count` is roughly double the request count, cardinality doubles, and filtering on `phase=body` silently drops exception observations (which are recorded with no phase).

The goal is to make both modules record the duration histogram exactly once per request (on response body completion, on exception, or on interceptor response) with no `phase` attribute, drop the now-unused `phase` parameter from the two internal response-attribute helpers, fix the doc comments that describe the phase attribute, note in server/core that the OpenTelemetry modules ignore `forResponsePhase`, and update tests so they assert one point per request and that the histogram count equals the number of requests. Prometheus, Datadog and ZIO metrics keep their `phase` label and are out of scope. This is a breaking change for anyone querying the OpenTelemetry duration histogram by `phase`; the PR description must say so and reference `Fixes #5542`.

- Change `private[otel4s] def responseAttrs(l, res, phase: Option[String])` to `responseAttrs(l, res)` and remove the line that adds the phase attribute. Update the three `responseAttrs(..., None)` call sites in `requestTotal` and the three `Some(labels.forResponsePhase.*)` call sites in `requestDuration`.

In `metrics/otel4s-metrics/src/test/scala/sttp/tapir/server/metrics/otel4s/Otel4sMetricsTest.scala`:

resultJson.brief:
## Modules involved

- `metrics/otel4s-metrics/` — tapir metrics for the typelevel otel4s library (`Meter[F]`, `Attributes` from `org.typelevel.otel4s`). Scala 2.13 + 3. sbt-projectmatrix ids: `otel4sMetrics`, `otel4sMetrics3`.
- `metrics/opentelemetry-metrics/` — tapir metrics for the OpenTelemetry Java API (`io.opentelemetry.api.metrics.Meter`, `io.opentelemetry.api.common.Attributes`). Scala 2.12 + 2.13 + 3. sbt ids: `opentelemetryMetrics2_12`, `opentelemetryMetrics`, `opentelemetryMetrics3`. Code must stay 2.12-compatible (test uses `scala.collection.JavaConverters._`, not `scala.jdk`).
- `server/core/src/main/scala/sttp/tapir/server/metrics/Metric.scala` — shared metric types: `Metric`, `EndpointMetric`, `MetricLabels`, `MetricLabelsTyped`, `ResponsePhaseLabel`. Used by every metrics backend.
- `doc/server/observability.md` — user docs. The OpenTelemetry section (lines 234–259) and otel4s section (261–308) do not mention `phase`. The word `phase` appears only at lines 108 and 192, inside the Prometheus sections. Nothing to change there.

## Files to change

### `metrics/otel4s-metrics/src/main/scala/sttp/tapir/server/metrics/otel4s/Otel4sMetrics.scala`
- `private def requestDuration[F[_]](meter: Meter[F], labels: MetricLabels): Metric[F, F[Histogram[F, Double]]]` (line ~133). Builds an `EndpointMetric()` with `.onResponseHeaders`, `.onResponseBody`, `.onException`, `.onInterceptorResponse`. Remove the `onResponseHeaders` block. The other three each call `recorder.record(duration, requestAttrs(...) ++ responseAttrs(...))`.
- `private[otel4s] def responseAttrs(l: MetricLabels, res: Either[Throwable, ServerResponse[_]], phase: Option[String]): Attributes` (line ~187). Drop the `phase` parameter and the `.addAll(phase.map(v => Attribute.from(l.forResponsePhase.name, v)))` line. Keep the `Attribute` import: it is still used by the type alias `private type MetricLabels = MetricLabelsTyped[Attribute[_]]`.
- Call sites of `responseAttrs` passing `None` in `requestTotal` (three, lines ~122–128) must also be updated.

### `metrics/otel4s-metrics/src/test/scala/sttp/tapir/server/metrics/otel4s/Otel4sMetricsTest.scala`
- Imports `Otel4sMetrics.{requestAttrs, responseAttrs}` and calls `responseAttrs(labels, Right(res), None)` / `responseAttrs(labels, Left(ex), None)` in the custom-gauge metric (lines ~210–211).
- `requestDurationExpectation(expectedCount, expectedStatusCode, isFailure)` (line ~273): success branch uses `.pointCount(2)` with two `containsPoints` for `phaseAttribute("headers")` and `phaseAttribute("body")`. Failure branch already uses `.pointCount(1)` with `PointExpectation.histogram.count(expectedCount.toLong)`. After the change both branches are the same shape: `pointCount(1)` and one point with `count(expectedCount.toLong)` and `attributesSubset(baseResponseAttributes(expectedStatusCode) ++ failureAttributes(isFailure))`. Remove `phaseAttribute` helper (line ~342).
- Test harness: `OtelJavaTestkit.inMemory[IO]()`, `testkit.collectMetrics`, `MetricExpectations.checkAll`. `PointExpectation.histogram.count(n)` asserts the histogram point's count, so the "count equals number of requests" check comes from the existing `expectedCount` (2 for the success test, 1 for error-response test, 2 for failure test). The `metricExpectation(HttpMetrics.ServerRequestDuration)` helper checks required semconv attributes are present on all points.
- Requests to `/human` do not match the endpoint and produce no metric (decode failure path).

### `metrics/opentelemetry-metrics/src/main/scala/sttp/tapir/server/metrics/opentelemetry/OpenTelemetryMetrics.scala`
- `def requestDuration[F[_]](meter: Meter, labels: MetricLabels): Metric[F, DoubleHistogram]` (line ~172), public. Same four callbacks; remove `onResponseHeaders`. Each callback wraps in `m.eval { ... recorder.record(duration, otLabels) }` where `otLabels = merge(asOpenTelemetryAttributes(labels, ep, req), asOpenTelemetryAttributes(labels, Right(res), Some(...)))`.
- `private def asOpenTelemetryAttributes(l: MetricLabels, res: Either[Throwable, ServerResponse[_]], phase: Option[String]): Attributes` (line ~237). Drop `phase` param and `phase.foreach(v => builder.put(l.forResponsePhase.name, v))`. There is an overload `asOpenTelemetryAttributes(l, ep: AnyEndpoint, req: ServerRequest)` for request+endpoint; overload resolution stays unambiguous after the change (2 args with `Either` vs 3 args).
- Call sites passing `None` in `requestTotal` (three, lines ~149–164) must be updated.
- Doc comments on `def default[F[_]](otel: OpenTelemetry)` (lines ~80–88) and `def default[F[_]](meter: Meter)` (lines ~95–103) each end with the sentence "The `phase` attribute is added to the duration histogram and can be either `headers` or `body` - request duration is measured separately up to the point where the headers are determined, and then once again when the whole response body is complete." Delete that sentence (and the blank scaladoc line before it) in both.

### `metrics/opentelemetry-metrics/src/test/scala/sttp/tapir/server/metrics/opentelemetry/OpenTelemetryMetricsTest.scala`
- Uses `InMemoryMetricReader`, `SdkMeterProvider`, `Identity` monad, `PersonsApi` from `sttp.tapir.server.TestUtil` (server/core test utils), `AnyFlatSpec`.
- "collect http.server.request.duration" test (line ~130): runs 3 requests via `interpret(100/200/300)` (a fresh `ServerInterpreter` each time, but the same `metrics`/histogram instrument), then reads `reader.collectAllMetrics().asScala.head.getHistogramData.getPoints.asScala` and asserts `points.map(_.getAttributes) should contain(Attributes.of(..., AttributeKey.stringKey("phase"), "body", ...))`. Remove the phase key/value pair. All 3 requests share identical attributes, so after the change there is exactly one point; assert `points should have size 1` and `points.head.getCount shouldBe 3` (`HistogramPointData.getCount` returns Long).
- "record request duration for interceptor response" test (line ~263): asserts phase=body at lines ~291–292 for a 405 response from `RejectInterceptor`. Remove the phase pair; optionally assert one point with count 1.
- `Attributes.of(...)` equality is order-independent (keys are sorted internally), so key ordering in the expected value does not matter.

### `server/core/src/main/scala/sttp/tapir/server/metrics/Metric.scala`
- `case class ResponsePhaseLabel(name: String, headersValue: String, bodyValue: String)` (line 48) has no doc comment. `forResponsePhase: ResponsePhaseLabel = ResponsePhaseLabel("phase", "headers", "body")` is a field on both `MetricLabels` (line 54) and `MetricLabelsTyped` (line 70). Add a short doc comment on `ResponsePhaseLabel` saying it is used by Prometheus, Datadog and ZIO metrics and ignored by `OpenTelemetryMetrics` and `Otel4sMetrics`. Keep the field and class; other backends reference it.

## Callback semantics (from `Metric.onRequest` doc in Metric.scala)
Exactly one callback sequence runs per request: `onEndpointRequest` → `onResponseHeaders` → `onResponseBody` (happy path), or `onEndpointRequest` → `onException`, or `onException`, or `onInterceptorResponse`, or `onDecodeFailure`. Recording only on `onResponseBody`, `onException`, `onInterceptorResponse` therefore yields exactly one histogram observation per request that produced a response.

## Build / test
- MiMa is disabled for all modules except core (`mimaPreviousArtifacts := Set.empty` in `commonSettings`, build.sbt line 77). Changing the `private[otel4s]` `responseAttrs` signature is safe.
- Verification command from the task: `sbt "opentelemetryMetrics/test" "opentelemetryMetrics3/test" "otel4sMetrics/test" "otel4sMetrics3/test"`; also `sbt opentelemetryMetrics2_12/compile` (or `opentelemetryMetrics2_12/Test/compile`). For the core doc comment, `sbt serverCore/compile` suffices.
- The OT module test "collect http.server.active_requests" uses `Thread.sleep(2000)`; the suite is slow but not flaky.

## Conventions (user CLAUDE.md)
- Comments only for what is not obvious from the code; keep them minimal and short. Never restate implementation in a comment.
- Never commit unless explicitly asked; never add Claude as co-author.
- PR description: short, simple language, state the breaking change for users querying the OpenTelemetry duration histogram by `phase`, include `Fixes #5542`.
- Do not create a migration doc. Do not touch Prometheus, Prometheus-simpleclient, Datadog or ZIO metrics modules.
